# heraut check runtime

Check git, its identity, the history and each release target's token.

Check what a release needs from this machine: git on PATH, git user.name and user.email, the full
history (not a shallow clone), and for each release target a token that can reach its API. A dirty
working tree is a warning, not a failure.

## Usage

```text
heraut check runtime [flags]
```

## Examples

```bash
heraut check runtime
heraut check runtime --env prod
```

## Flags

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--env <string>` |  | target environment (for per-env strategies) |
| `--json` |  | print the result as a JSON envelope |

## Global flags

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--config <string>` |  | path to .heraut.yml (default: auto-discover) |
| `--verbose` |  | echo each command and emit diagnostic logs |
